page.layout: One printed page, single column. At the top, a decorative border of ornaments (not text). Below it, the section number II, then a six-line... [seven-line] verse stanza in italic, a right-set dedication paragraph with a signature line, the word FINIS, and a woodcut of flowers in a vase at the foot. No running head, page number, catchword or signature.

p.i: UNde tibi quæso, dicas, hîc suppetit ardor? Quo vel ad arma omnes nunc pacis tempore poscis: Quid te commoveat, video; nec spes, puto, fallit: Gloria nonne Dei tibi dat certaminis ansam? Ad gratos igitur lætus contende triumphos, Nec dubites, cedat quin mox victoria vobis, Cùm tibi sit clypeus summus moderator Olympi.

main_text.p: Hæc paucula in honoris & amicitiæ in-æternum duraturæ τεκμήριον accine-re voluit
V. H. S. S. M. Cand.

page.notes: The initial U of the verse is a large woodcut-style letter joined to "Nde", so it is written as "UNde". The Greek word τεκμήριον is printed in the dedication; the breathings and accent may be uncertain at this scan resolution. The woodcut at the foot (flowers in a vase) and the ornamental border at the top are not text and are not transcribed. Faint show-through text from the reverse page is visible in the background and is left out.
